title: Token-Pulse Microwindow Scheduler with NCCL-Overlap Hints and Kernel Affinity
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Background: We observe tail-latency spikes and throughput cliffs when prefill and decode workloads interleave on heterogeneous GPU pools. Existing windowed rendezvous approaches reduce worst-case stalls but are brittle under varying device bandwidth and attention-kernel choices. This ticket introduces a Token-Pulse Microwindow Scheduler (TPMS): a latency-driven microwindow allocator that hedges with small, adaptive prefetch windows, emits NCCL-overlap hints to the comm layer, and applies kernel-affinity planning per microwindow. The goal is to reduce 95/99 p99 prefill+decode latencies while preserving overall throughput and avoiding global synchronization points.

Scope: Implement scheduler logic in the runtime request router and conductor. Add kernel-affinity planner that tags microwindows with preferred kernel/quantization variants and a lightweight NCCL overlap hint that the NCCL orchestration layer can use to opportunistically pipeline collectives. Integrate backpressure telemetry and prefix-cache warm signals. Experiment with microwindow sizes from 2-16 tokens and dynamic skewing across stages to minimize inter-GPU stalls.

Out-of-scope: Full redesign of NCCL; heavy-weight topology rebalancing; new quantization formats beyond existing runtime support.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end latency for mixed prefill+decode test workload reduced by >=15% versus baseline (runtime-2.3) under 75% cluster load
No regression in average throughput (tokens/s) beyond 5% for steady-state decoder-only workloads
Graceful fallback: when NCCL overlap hints are unsupported or GPU topology changes, scheduler falls back to conservative microwindowing without correctness issues
Unit and integration tests for microwindow allocator, kernel-affinity tag transport, and NCCL hint plumbing in CI
Feature gated behind runtime flag and controlled rollout via canary lanes in Dedicated
tasks: Design: propose microwindow sizing heuristic and kernel-affinity tagging scheme (owner: Aisha)
Prototype: scheduler prototype in dev runtime branch that emits microwindow assignments and NCCL hints (owner: Ravi)
Kernel affinity: extend kernel selector to accept microwindow tags and prefer fast fused-attention kernels when latency trade-off favored (owner: Mei)
Comm integration: add NCCL-overlap hint consumer that schedules asynchronous collectives when safe (owner: Jordan)
Telemetry: add metrics for microwindow utilization, overlap success rate, and per-stage stall time (owner: Priya)

Docs: update dev docs and release notes with configuration knobs and troubleshooting steps (owner: Docs)

benchmarks: Baseline runtime-2.3 mixed workload: p95=138ms, p99=312ms, tokens/s=42k
Early prototype (dev branch): p95=118ms (-14%), p99=270ms (-13%), tokens/s=40.5k (-3.6%)
Optimized kernel-affinity enabled: p95=106ms (-23%), p99=240ms (-23%), tokens/s=41.3k (-1.6%)
risks: Aggressive microwindowing can reduce effective batching, increasing per-token compute cost
Incorrect NCCL-overlap hinting may create communication contention and worsen tail latency on some topologies
Kernel-affinity tags add complexity to kernel selector and increase testing surface for rare model shapes
Feature could interact poorly with Dedicated autoscaler if not surfaced to capacity planner
decisions: Microwindow size will be adaptive, starting default at 8 tokens and shrinking under high tail latency to 4 tokens; will not exceed 16 tokens
Kernel-affinity is advisory: runtime kernel selector may override based on local memory pressure metrics
NCCL-overlap hint is a best-effort opt-in contract between runtime and comm layer; will be disabled on known-unsupported GPU topologies
Expose three knobs: target_microwindow_tokens, overlap_aggressiveness (0-3), and kernel_affinity_mode (off|advisory|strict)
